audit_items.proof_trace: The admin check (is_admin guard at L28-30) is enforced only at the Next.js HTTP route layer; no SQL migration files exist so the delete_application RPC's internal authorization is unverifiable. The RPC is called with only p_id (no user context parameter), unlike delete_user_consent which passes p_user_id for DB-level ownership enforcement, suggesting no caller identity check inside the function. Supabase exposes all RPCs via PostgREST at /rest/v1/rpc/delete_application, meaning an authenticated non-admin user can call the function directly with their JWT, bypassing the application-layer guard entirely.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An authenticated but non-admin club member sends POST /rest/v1/rpc/delete_application with body {"p_id": "<target-client-id>"} and their Supabase JWT; if delete_application grants EXECUTE to the authenticated role and lacks an internal auth.uid()/is_admin check, the OAuth client is deleted without the Next.js admin gate ever being invoked.
